title: SetResponse uses std::collections::HashMap; non-deterministic iteration; inconsistent with extras serde_json::Map choice
description:
crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:274-286 declares `SetResponse<T>`
fields:

    pub created: Option<HashMap<String, T>>,
    pub updated: Option<HashMap<Id, Option<T>>>,
    pub not_created: Option<HashMap<String, SetError>>,
    pub not_updated: Option<HashMap<Id, SetError>>,
    pub not_destroyed: Option<HashMap<Id, SetError>>,

`HashMap` is `std::collections::HashMap`. Three coupled consequences:

1. **Non-deterministic iteration order.** A client logging
   `for (id, err) in &resp.not_created { ... }` will see the entries
   in random order between runs. The exact same wire payload may be
   logged as `[a, b, c]` on Monday and `[c, a, b]` on Tuesday. This
   leaks through to integration tests that compare log output, to
   bug reports that paste log snippets, and to operator dashboards
   that depend on stable ordering.

2. **Inconsistent with the extras pattern.** This crate has just
   migrated `SetError.extra` from `HashMap` to `serde_json::Map`
   (commit 9c66783) explicitly for deterministic serialized output
   (the rustdoc on `SetError.extra` says so — see methods.rs:194-196,
   though that doc-comment lies about the *mechanism*; cf. JMAP-6xs8.10).
   The same struct that contains those `HashMap`s also contains an
   `extra: serde_json::Map`. Two different choices for two different
   maps on the same type. A reader cannot deduce the principle.

3. **Public type leaks the storage choice.** Once shipped, the
   maintainer cannot replace `HashMap` with `IndexMap`,
   `BTreeMap`, or `serde_json::Map` without breaking every caller
   that has `let map: &HashMap<Id, _> = resp.not_updated.as_ref().unwrap()`.
   The choice committed at 0.1.1 is a forever commitment.

What a caller depending on this API in production accepts:
- Non-deterministic iteration in logs, dashboards, and tests.
- The need to wrap iteration in `let mut entries: Vec<_> = map.iter().collect(); entries.sort_by_key(|(id, _)| id.clone());` boilerplate any time they want stable output.
- No future hardening to a deterministic map type without major bump.

Fix candidates:
- Replace `HashMap` with `serde_json::Map<String, T>` (where keys
  serialize as strings) for consistency with extras. Iterates in
  lexicographic key order under default features. Wire-compatible.
- Or: replace with `BTreeMap<Id, T>` / `BTreeMap<String, T>`. Same
  benefit, std-only. Wire-compatible.
- Or: introduce a workspace newtype `pub struct SetMap<K, V>(BTreeMap<K, V>)`
  and use it everywhere.

The same finding applies to `JmapRequest.created_ids` and
`JmapResponse.created_ids` (`Option<HashMap<Id, Id>>` in wire.rs).
Same justification.
close_reason: Done: SetResponse maps are BTreeMap (crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:26,359-371); created_ids is BTreeMap<Id,Id> (wire.rs:5,77,100)
